info.description: PRATIKSHYA FASHON — Feature-Based Backend API for Customer, Employee, and Admin surfaces.

Body: `{ refresh_token }`

Rotates the refresh token (old one is blacklisted) and issues a new access token, re-reading the employee's current roles.

**Two allowed paths:**

1. **Bootstrap** (no active admins exist) — anyone may call this. Gated by `ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_SECRET` if that env var is set.

2. **Privileged** (admins already exist) — requires a `SUPER_ADMIN` JWT or the bootstrap secret.

get.description:
Authorization: `products.view`.  
Filters: `status`, `category`, `subcategory`, `assignedEmployeeId`, `q` (name / SKU / id / label / taxonomy / fabric).

post.summary: Admin — create draft with caller-supplied permanent ID
post.description:
Authorization: `products.manage`.  
Body: `{ id, ...full supported product fields }`.  
ID must match `^[A-Z0-9][A-Z0-9-]{1,35}$` (covers the canonical `PF-<DEPT>-<FAMILY>-<SUB>-NNNN` ids) and be unique — a taken ID is a 409.  
Lifecycle/unsupported keys are rejected; every other supported field is persisted in the same call.

get.summary: Admin — deterministic next stable product id
get.description:
Source: `nextStableProductId()`.  
Query: `category={categoryId}&preferredNumber={n}` (optional).  
Never random; scans the register and picks the lowest free integer.  
Canonical form: `PF-{CATEGORY_CODE}-{NNNN}` (four-digit serial).

get.summary: Admin — check SKU and slug availability
get.description:
Query: `sku=&slug=&excludeId=`. Returns `{ skuTaken, slugTaken, suggestedSlug? }`.  
Pre-flight only — the authoritative uniqueness verdict is the **409 `CONFLICT`** raised by the create/update endpoints, which use the same trimmed, case-insensitive comparison. Pass `excludeId` when editing an existing product so its own SKU/slug is reported as free.

post.description:
Authorization: `products.manage`.  
Precondition: product is pending review.  
Effect: `review.state = APPROVED`; visibility stays PENDING_REVIEW. Going live requires the separate, gated publish action.

Body: `{ reason: string }`.  
Effect: `status = DRAFT`, `review.state = REJECTED`, `rejectionReason = reason`.

Authorization: `products.manage`.  
Preconditions: review approved (`review.state == APPROVED`) AND no unresolved `getPublishIssues()`. Effect: `status = PUBLISHED`, `published = true`, `published_by/_at` recorded.
Effect: `status = ARCHIVED`. **Removes the product from every customer surface** until restored. This must be surfaced to the operator before confirming.

get.description: Returns `{ issues: string[] }` — the same list that `approve` and `publish` check. Non-empty ⇒ the action buttons are disabled in the UI.

post.description:
Body: `{ newId }` — validated `^[A-Z0-9][A-Z0-9-]{1,35}$`, must be free.  
Activity `PRODUCT_RENAMED_ID`.  
**Cascade question resolved (plan §24 step 8):** this route rewrites the human-facing **display label** (`productId`) only — never `catalog_product.id`, the primary key that media, inventory, collection membership and order history reference. No cascade is required, and none is performed. `newId` must collide with neither an existing primary key nor another product's display label, otherwise **409 `CONFLICT`**.
Creates a `DRAFT` copy with a new runtime id. Activity `PRODUCT_DUPLICATED`.

Body: `{ flags: string[] }` — each flag must be a member of the declared review-flag vocabulary (plan §24 step 8); an unknown flag is a **422 `VALIDATION_ERROR`** naming it. Blocking flags: `NAME_REVIEW_REQUIRED`, `PRICE_REVIEW_REQUIRED`, `TAXONOMY_REVIEW_REQUIRED`, `GROUP_REVIEW_REQUIRED`, `VARIANT_REVIEW_REQUIRED`, `NEEDS_MEDIA`, `MEDIA_OWNERSHIP_REVIEW`, `CONFLICT_UNRESOLVED`, `KIDS_MIGRATION_REVIEW`. Informational flags: `CONFLICT_REVIEW_LATER`, `MEDIA_OWNERSHIP_MOVED`, `MEDIA_UNASSIGNED`.  
Activity `PRODUCT_REVIEW_FLAGS_CLEARED`.

patch.description:
Authorization: `products.manage` AND `product.assignedEmployeeId === employee.employeeId` (SUPER_ADMIN bypasses).

Unsupported fields are rejected with the canonical 422 validation envelope.

post.summary: Admin — activate a DRAFT category (DRAFT → ACTIVE)
post.description:
Authorization: `categories.edit`.  
Activation is the promotion step for categories created by the admin desk (creation always starts in DRAFT so an unfinished category is never surfaced to customers).  
Only `DRAFT` categories can be activated; `ARCHIVED` uses restore.

Authorization: `categories.archive`.  
**CRITICAL**: Archiving removes ALL products in this category from every customer surface (the visibility gate reads category status).  
The operator must confirm this before calling.  
Activity: `CATEGORY_ARCHIVED`.

get.description:
Which provider is active, the application-level media URL prefix, and
whether a CDN is configured. Credentials and filesystem paths are never
part of this payload.

post.summary: Resolve product image references to canonical media URLs
post.description:
Batch resolution decisions.

Each entry reports `status` — `resolved`, `legacy-fallback`,
`passthrough`, `empty` or `disabled` — so the migration's dual-read
behaviour is observable instead of silent.

get.description:
Return the bytes of a single object inside the configured media store.

404 when the key is legal but absent; 422 when the key is not legal.

delete.description:
Delete exactly one explicitly named object.

There is no cascade and no garbage collection in this phase: an object is
only removed when an administrator names it. The original
`frontend/public/images` assets are outside the storage root and can
never be reached from here.

get.summary: Resolved media set for one product
get.description:
The product's media set — BOTH halves of the Phase 7 dual-read.

Legacy half (unchanged): the product's own authored columns (`image`,
`hover_image`, `additional_images`) resolved through the storage layer.

Registered half (Phase 7 source of truth for NEW media): the durable
`media_product_media` associations joined to their `media_media_asset`
rows, ordered primary-first — each with its object key and canonical
`/media/objects/...` URL. A product with no registered rows answers
exactly as it did before this phase.

post.description:
Store one image in the object store and return its canonical URL.

The object key is derived from real identity (`products/{PRODUCT_ID}/
{filename}`), never from a random temp name. Nothing is written to the
database: persisting the reference onto a product uses the existing
`PATCH /admin/products/{id}` media fields.

`namespace` is validated against the closed storage vocabulary
(`app.storage.keys.ALLOWED_NAMESPACES`); an unknown namespace is a 422
`BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` and no object is written.

post.summary: Upload a media object for a product (admin)
post.description: Upload scoped to one product — the key namespace cannot be spoofed.

post.summary: Register an uploaded object as a media asset
post.description:
Create the durable row only after verifying the real object exists.

Idempotent by object key: re-registering the same key returns the same
asset row and UPDATES the existing product association's role / sort
order / primary flag instead of duplicating it. When `is_primary` is set,
every other association of the same product is demoted in the same
transaction — a product never has two primaries.

`role` is checked against the declared product-media vocabulary before
anything is written. Before plan §24 step 9 this column accepted any
string: the value went straight into a `String(30)` column, so a long
role was an HTTP 500 (`StringDataRightTruncation`) on PostgreSQL rather
than a validation rejection.

get.summary: Get current customer profile, addresses, preferences & sessions
get.description:
Returns `{ profile, addresses[], preferences, security: { activeSessions[] } }`. Authorization: Customer session (Bearer token).

**BACKEND_GAP (documented):** the access token carries no session id claim, so the caller's session cannot be identified — every `activeSessions[]` entry is returned with `isCurrent: false`. The frontend renders these as active sessions without a current-device badge. Remediation: mint a `sid` claim at issue time and pass it through (the service already accepts it).

patch.description: Accepts any subset of `{ firstName, lastName, email, phone, dateOfBirth, avatar }`. Authorization: Customer session.
Body: `{ emailNotifications, smsNotifications, promotionalUpdates, orderUpdates, stylingInvitations }` — all boolean, all optional. Authorization: Customer session.

post.summary: Sign out all other active sessions
post.description:
Revokes active sessions for the customer. Authorization: Customer session.

**BACKEND_GAP (documented):** the access token carries no session id claim, so the calling session cannot be excluded — this currently revokes **ALL** active sessions, including the one making the request (the caller is signed out everywhere). The frontend states this on the security page instead of promising 'other devices only'. Remediation: mint a `sid` claim at issue time and pass it through (the service already accepts the current-session argument).

get.description:
Returns `{ items, count, totals, coupon, coupon_lapsed }`.  

**Restore rules applied on every read:**  
- Drop lines whose product is deleted or unpublished.  
- Clamp quantity to available stock.  
- Merge duplicate `(productId, color, size)` lines.  
- Invalidate lapsed coupons (`coupon_lapsed = true`).

delete.description: Removes all lines and detaches any applied coupon.

post.description:
Body: `{ productId, color?, size?, quantity }`.  

**Line identity:** `(productId, color, size)`. Same triple → same line; quantities add.  

Validates product is `PUBLISHED` and has stock. Clamps to available stock if requested quantity exceeds it.

patch.description:
Body: `{ quantity }`.  
`quantity < 1` removes the line entirely.  
`lineId` is the SHA-1 hash of `productId::color::size` (returned as `id` in each cart item).

delete.description: Removes the cart line identified by `lineId`.

post.description:
Body: `{ code }`.  

**Validation checks:**  
- Coupon exists and is active.  
- Within valid date window.  
- Global usage limit not reached.  
- Per-customer limit not reached.  
- Customer is in the eligibility list (if set).  
- Cart subtotal ≥ minimum order value.  

Response: `{ ok: true, coupon, message: '<CODE> is now part of your order.' }`

get.description:
Returns `{ subtotal, productDiscount, couponDiscount, couponCode, offerId, shipping, codFee, total, saved }`.  

Query params:  
- `deliveryMethod`: `standard` (default) | `express`  
- `paymentMethod`: `online` (default) | `cod`  

**Pricing constants (authoritative, shared with the order boundary):**  
- Free shipping threshold: ₹5,000 (standard only — express is never free)  
- Standard shipping fee: ₹99  
- Express shipping fee: ₹199  
- COD surcharge: ₹49

Returns `{ ok: true, items: [productId], count }`.  
Authorization: Customer JWT.  
Creates an empty wishlist on first access.

post.description:
Adds `productId` to the wishlist. Calling this again for the same product is a no-op.  

The product must exist and be storefront-visible (`PUBLISHED` and published) — an unknown or unavailable product is a 404.  
Returns the updated `{ ok: true, items, count }`.

delete.description:
Removes `productId` from the wishlist. No-op if the product was not saved.  
Returns the updated `{ ok: true, items, count }`.

post.description:
Adds the product if it is not currently saved (requiring it to exist and be storefront-visible); removes it if it is.  
Returns the updated `{ ok: true, items, count }`.

get.description: Returns all currently active (non-archived) coupons/offers. Authorization: public.

post.summary: Validate a coupon code — the single checkout gate
post.description:
Body: `{ code, cartItems[], customerId?, customerEmail? }`.  

**This is the one gate through which every discount must pass.** No other code path may grant a discount.  

Response success: `{ ok: true, coupon, discount }`.  
Response failure: `{ ok: false, error: 'Human readable message.' }`.

get.summary: Admin — list offers/coupons with filters and pagination
get.description:
Authorization: `offers.view`. Returns all offers including ARCHIVED.  
Filters: `q` (code/name substring), `status` (`ACTIVE|SCHEDULED|EXPIRED|ARCHIVED`, evaluated from is_active/dates).  
Pagination: `page` + `pageSize`; `total` is the full filtered count.

post.description: Authorization: `offers.create`. Code is uppercased and must be unique — duplicates are rejected with **409**, invalid discount windows with **422**.

get.description: Authorization: `offers.view`. Resolves inactive/expired rows too.

patch.description: Authorization: `offers.edit`. Partial patch — only provided fields are written; `usage_count` is never client-writable. Changing `code` re-runs the uniqueness check (409 on collision).

post.description: Authorization: `offers.edit`.

Authorization: `offers.edit`.  
**Persistence boundary**: the coupon table has no separate paused flag, so pause archives the row's visibility (`is_active=false`); a paused and an archived offer are stored identically and re-activation is the same endpoint either way. The UI says exactly this.
Authorization: `offers.archive` (SUPER_ADMIN only — the ADMIN role does not carry this permission). Same persisted effect as pause; kept as a distinct route for the permission difference.

Creates a Razorpay order for online payments (UPI/card/netbanking) and returns the `razorpayOrderId` + `razorpayKeyId` needed to open the Razorpay checkout modal on the frontend.  

**Canonical flow (Phase 2):** the order is created first (`POST /orders` → `PENDING_PAYMENT`), then this session. The charge amount is the order's authoritative server-computed total — client drafts are rejected. **COD** orders do not use payment sessions.  

**Ownership:** the caller must own the order (authenticated customer, or the order's own guest email via `guestEmail`).  

**Idempotency:** pass `idempotencyKey` to safely retry; an existing active session for the order is resumed instead of duplicated.  

**Auth:** Customer session or guest (guest email required for guest orders).

get.description:
Returns the current status of a payment session.  

Status lifecycle: `CREATED → PENDING → PAID | FAILED | CANCELLED | EXPIRED`  

**Ownership:** the caller must own the session's order — authenticated customer, or the order's guest email via the `guestEmail` query parameter.

post.description:
Cancels a payment session that is in `CREATED` or `PENDING` status.  

Sessions in terminal states (`PAID`, `FAILED`, `CANCELLED`, `EXPIRED`) cannot be cancelled.  

**Ownership is required:** authenticated customer, or the order's guest email via `guestEmail` in the request body.

Called by the frontend immediately after `razorpay.open()` returns a successful payment callback.  

**Security:** Recomputes HMAC-SHA256 of `razorpay_order_id + '|' + razorpay_payment_id` using `RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET` and compares it (constant-time) against the provided `razorpay_signature`.  

Additionally fetches the payment from Razorpay to cross-check the amount matches the order total.  

On success: the session and order move to `PAID`, and the order transitions `PENDING_PAYMENT → PAYMENT_CONFIRMED → ORDER_CONFIRMED`.  
On failure: returns HTTP 422 and marks the session as `FAILED`.  

**Ownership:** the caller must own the order — authenticated customer, or the order's guest email via `guestEmail`. A client can never mark an order `PAID` without a valid signature + ownership.  

**Auth:** Customer session or guest (guest email required for guest orders).

Receives signed webhook events from Razorpay.  

**Security:** The `X-Razorpay-Signature` header is verified as HMAC-SHA256 of the **raw request body** using `RAZORPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. Requests with a missing or invalid signature are rejected with HTTP 403.  

Supported events:  
- `payment.captured` → session + order set to `PAID`  
- `payment.failed` → session + order set to `FAILED`  
- `order.paid` → idempotent confirmation  

All handlers are idempotent — Razorpay may deliver events more than once.  

**IMPORTANT:** Raw bytes are read BEFORE any JSON parsing to ensure the HMAC covers exactly the bytes that Razorpay signed.

post.description:
Authorization: **Customer session or guest** (guest orders are claimable later via the verified-email claim flow).  

**Initial state (payment method ≠ payment state):**  
- COD → `status = ORDER_CONFIRMED`, `paymentStatus = PENDING` (cash collected on delivery; no online payment session)  
- UPI / card / netbanking → `status = PENDING_PAYMENT`, `paymentStatus = PENDING` (only server-side Razorpay verification/webhook can mark it PAID)  
- `statusHistory` seeded: `PENDING_PAYMENT → PAYMENT_CONFIRMED → ORDER_CONFIRMED`  
- `timeline` seeded: `ORDER_CREATED`, `PAYMENT_CONFIRMED`, `ORDER_CONFIRMED`  

**Pricing (authoritative, server-computed):**  
- Prices resolved from the catalogue — client totals/prices/discounts are not accepted  
- Free shipping threshold: ₹5,000 · Standard: ₹99 · Express: ₹199 (never free) · COD surcharge: ₹49  
- Coupon revalidated server-side (active / dates / usage limits / eligibility / minimum order)  

**Stock:** validated and reserved under row locks in this transaction.  

**Idempotency:** optional `idempotencyKey` — a retried attempt returns the same order.

get.summary: Product search — full-text + faceted, sorted and paginated

Matching is case/diacritic-normalised substring — exactly reproduces `matchesSearch()` / `normaliseSearchText()` from the frontend.  

**Visibility gate** — only `PUBLISHED` products in an `ACTIVE` category and, when set, an `ACTIVE` subcategory.  

**Facets** — 12 facets (category, subcategory, gender, price, size, color, fabric, material, occasion, collection, rating, availability). Multi-value: repeat the key. AND across facets, OR within a facet.  

**Sort** — recommended (default), newest, price-asc, price-desc, discount, name-asc, popularity, rating. Aliases: price-low → price-asc, price-high → price-desc, name/az → name-asc.  

**Pagination** — `page` + `pageSize` (default 20, max 200).  

**Suggestions** — static list today; dynamic suggest is `BACKEND DECISION REQUIRED`.

get.summary: Explore — paginated product stream with interleaved promo/editorial cards
get.description:
The **only** paginated surface in the application (pageSize defaults to 20).  

Returns `items` (the plain product page) plus `stream` — the same products interleaved with `promo` and `editorial` cards at fixed intervals:  
- A **promo** card is inserted after every 4th product (`EXPLORE_PROMO_AFTER`).  
- An **editorial** card is inserted after every 8th product (`EXPLORE_EDITORIAL_AFTER`).  
  When both intervals coincide the editorial card wins.  

**Visibility gate** — only `PUBLISHED` products in an `ACTIVE` category and, when set, an `ACTIVE` subcategory.  

**Facets, sort, pagination** — same vocabulary as `GET /products`.  

**`hasMore`** — `true` when `page × pageSize < total`.

Returns the promotional offer strip displayed inside the explore stream.  
Source: `getExploreOffers()`.  
Content is static today; a live offer table is `BACKEND DECISION REQUIRED`.

Single endpoint that assembles the full homepage:  
- **heroSlides** — hero carousel slides (media URLs are `BACKEND DECISION REQUIRED`).  
- **newArrivals** — up to 12 newest `PUBLISHED` products.  
- **categories** — shop-by-category cards derived from active product categories.  
- **sareeEdit** — up to 8 saree products.  
- **brideGroomEdit** — up to 4 bridal couture + 4 menswear products.  
- **celebrationEdit** — up to 8 festive-occasion products.  
- **saleBanner** — sale banner seam.  

**Reservation rule** — hero media plates are reserved first; every subsequent seam skips images already used by an earlier section so no plate appears twice on the page. `BACKEND DECISION REQUIRED`: composed endpoint vs several separate endpoints — the reservation ordering must be preserved either way.

TrackingEvent.title: TrackingEvent
TrackingEvent.description:
A real, recorded order event.

Every event returned by the tracking endpoint is a persisted
`orders_order_status_history` row — its `timestamp` is the stored
`created_at`, never a projected or estimated value. No carrier event
feed exists in this system, so no carrier events are ever synthesised.

TrackingResponse.title: TrackingResponse
TrackingResponse.description:
Order tracking, backed exclusively by stored order data.

`carrier` / `tracking_number` / `estimated_delivery` are the values an
admin recorded on dispatch (`POST /admin/orders/{id}/dispatch`); they
are `null` until that happens. `carrier_tracking_available` states
honestly whether a shipment identity exists, and
`carrier_events_available` is always `false` — no courier integration
exists in this system.

UpdateCouponRequest.title: UpdateCouponRequest
UpdateCouponRequest.description:
PATCH /admin/offers/{id} — mirrors the full CREATOR contract, all optional.

Any field the create endpoint accepts can be edited (including `code`,
`discount_type` and the eligibility/exclusion lists). `usage_count` is
never client-writable. Unknown keys are ignored — never persisted.

guestEmail.title: Guestemail
guestEmail.description: Guest order owner email (required for guest-owned orders)

VerifyPaymentRequest.title: VerifyPaymentRequest
VerifyPaymentRequest.description:
POST /payments/verify

The frontend sends these three values after a successful Razorpay.open()
callback so the backend can recompute and verify the HMAC-SHA256 signature.

The signature is the ONLY trust anchor — a client can never mark an
order PAID by sending a status flag. `guest_email` (guest checkout) is
checked against the order's own guest email so a caller cannot verify a
payment for an order they do not own.
